newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends off on world prices, crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends off on world prices, crop forecast.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed weaker on Friday, pressured by competitive world wheat prices and a private U.S. wheat production forecast that was above USDA's August estimate, traders said.
"The market still has more room to move to the downside as it tries to align itself with world wheat prices,' a KCBT trader said.
Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Cos. estimated 1996/97 total U.S. wheat production at 2.333 billion bushels, traders said. That figure was above USDA's August estimate of 2.249 billion bushels.
Losses were extended late as market-on-close sell orders came in, traders said. The bearish momentum was linked to corn/wheat and corn/soy spreads, traders said.
"They were buying the corn and beans and selling K.C.," a trader said.
Wheat closed 1/4 to 9-1/2 cents per bushel lower with September down 3-1/2 at $4.50-1/2 a bushel.
